propositions: Compaction writes SNAPSHOT.json and *.retired files and renames sources to *.retired without transaction rollback; if the detached sweep worker is killed before commit, untracked files remain in the working tree.

When reconverge runs git merge origin/tickets, if a peer has already pushed those same *.retired and SNAPSHOT paths to origin, the merge must create them but finds them already untracked in the working tree, causing git to abort with 'untracked working tree files would be overwritten by merge'.

The abort handler in _union_merge is abort-only and push-recovery cannot clear untracked files (git reset --hard is tracked-only, git stash without -u skips untracked), so every retry re-aborts identically and the store wedges permanently with local commits stranded off origin.

The fix detects the specific untracked-overwrite abort signature, parses the exact paths git names, relocates only those paths to a quarantine directory outside the worktree, and retries the merge once; on success both parents are kept and no local commit is orphaned.
Genuine content conflicts and any other merge failures fall back to today's abort-only behavior, keeping local state and logging the recovery hint unchanged.
Untracked files not named by git (including .tmp-event-* at tracker root and any runtime marker not on origin) are never quarantined and remain untouched.
